De caeco et Zacchaeo (olim sub auctore Joanne Chrysostomo)
Εἰς τὸν τυφλὸν, ὃν ὁ Χριστὸς ἐθεράπευσεν, καὶ εἰς τὸν Ζακχαῖον, καὶ
περὶ κρίσεως, καὶ ἐλεημοσύνης, ὁμιλία.
Πολλαὶ καὶ διάφοροι τῶν ἁγίων Γραφῶν αἱ διδασκαλίαι, μία δὲ χάρις ἡ πᾶσιν
ἐπιλάμπουσα, καὶ μία πηγὴ διδασκαλίας τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας. Καὶ ὅσα νόμος
διαγορεύει, καὶ ὅσα προφῆται διδάσκουσιν, ὅσα ἀπόστολοι κηρύττουσιν, ὅσα τὸ
Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς εὐσεβείας ὑπαγορεύει, ἀπὸ μιᾶς ὥσπερ τινὸς εὐθαλοῦς πηγῆς καὶ
γονίμου περιέρχεται, τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου· καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν οὔτε εἰπεῖν τι σεμνὸν,
οὔτε νοῆσαι δεξιὸν, οὔτε πρᾶξαι θαυμαστὸν, μὴ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος
ἐπιβεβαιοῦντος τὰ λεγόμενα, καὶ τὰ νοούμενα, καὶ τὰ πραττόμενα. Κἂν γάρ τις τῇ
ἀνθρωπίνῃ σοφίᾳ κομᾷ, καὶ λογισμοῖς ἀνθρωπίνοις ὠχυρωμένην ἔχῃ τὴν ψυχὴν,
τὸν λόγον δὲ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀποσείηται, εἰς οὐδέν ἐστι, καὶ εἰς οὐδὲν λογισθήσεται. ∆ιὰ
τοῦτό φησιν ὁ προφήτης· Τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου ἀπεποιήσαντο. Σοφία τίς ἐστιν ἐν
αὐτοῖς; Ἡμῖν τοίνυν ἄνθη τῆς ἀληθείας αἱ Γραφαὶ τῆς εὐσεβείας· καὶ πολλὰ μὲν τὰ
ἄνθη, εἷς δὲ ὁ λειμὼν ὁ τὰ ἄνθη τρέφων· πολλοὶ τῆς διδασκαλίας οἱ λαμπτῆρες, εἷς
δὲ ὁ φωστὴρ ὁ ἀληθινός· πολλοὶ οἱ ἀστέρες, εἷς δὲ ὁ οὐρανὸς ὁ φέρων τοὺς ἀστέρας·
πολλοὶ οἱ κλάδοι, μία δὲ ἡ ῥίζα· πολλοὶ οἱ δάκτυλοι, μία δὲ ἡ χεὶρ, ἡ διὰ τῶν
δακτύλων γράφουσα· πολλαὶ αἱ χορδαὶ, μία ἡ κιθάρα τοῦ Πνεύματος· πολλαὶ
διδασκαλίαι, μία ἡ πηγὴ τῆς εὐσεβείας. Ἀλλὰ θαυμάζω πῶς ὁ τυφλὸς οὗτος, οὐ
νόμον ἀναγνοὺς, οὐ προφήτας διελθὼν, οὐκ Εὐαγγελίοις ἐντυχὼν, οὐκ ἀποστόλοις
βεβαιωθεὶς, ἐπεκαλεῖτο τὸν Σωτῆρα τῆς οἰκουμένης, λέγων, Ἰησοῦ, υἱὲ ∆αυῒδ,
ἐλέησόν με. Πόθεν ἔμαθες ταῦτα καλεῖν, μὴ μαθὼν ὃ ἐπικαλῇ; Οὐκ ἀνέγνως βίβλους,
τῶν ὄψεων ἀπεστερημένος· οὐκ ἐσχόλασας διδασκαλίαις, μίαν ἔχων ὑπόθεσιν τῆς
ζωῆς, τὴν αἴτησιν, μᾶλλον δὲ τὸ προσαιτεῖν· πόθεν οὖν ἔγνως τὸν φωστῆρα τοῦ
κόσμου, ὃν οὔτε 59.600 ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἐθεάσω, οὔτε ἐπὶ γῆς, τῶν ὄψεων ἐστερημένος;
Ἀλλ' ἀληθῶς ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἐπληροῦτο τὸ ὑπὸ τοῦ ∆αυῒδ εἰρημένον· Κύριος σοφοῖ τοὺς
τυφλούς. Ὄχλος πολὺς ἦν περὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ὁ τυφλὸς τὸν μὲν φωστῆρα τῆς
ἀληθείας οὐκ ᾔδει, τῆς δὲ ἐνεργείας ᾔσθετο· ἥρπασε τῇ διαθέσει, ὃ μὴ παρέλαβεν ἡ
ὄψις. Τί, φησὶ, βούλεται ὁ ὄχλος; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ, Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος παρέρχεται. Ὢ
τοῦ θαύματος! ἄλλα διδάσκεται, καὶ ἄλλα κηρύττει· ἀκούει Ἰησοῦν Ναζωραῖον, οὐ
καλεῖ δὲ αὐτὸν Ἰησοῦν Ναζωραῖον, ἀλλ' Ἰησοῦν υἱὸν ∆αυΐδ. Οἱ βλέποντες τὰ ἐξ
ὑπονοίας ἔλεγον, ὁ δὲ τυφλὸς τὰ ἐξ ἀληθείας ἐκήρυττεν. Ἰησοῦ, υἱὲ ∆αυῒδ, ἐλέησόν
με. Τοίνυν ἕκαστος τὴν φωνὴν ἰδιοποιούμενος, ῥήξῃ ἀπὸ τῆς καρδίας ἐξομολόγησιν,
καὶ ἕκαστος ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ ταύτην εἴπῃ τὴν φωνὴν, Υἱὲ ∆αυῒδ, ἐλέησόν με. Καὶ ὥσπερ,
ἀδελφοὶ, ἐπειδὰν εἰς πένθος πολλοὶ ἀπέλθωσι, καὶ ἴδωσι σκήνωμα προκείμενον, καὶ
δακρυόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν ἰδίων, πάντες δακρύουσιν, οἱ μὲν συνδιατιθέμενοι τῷ πένθει,
οἱ δὲ τὰ ἑαυτῶν ἐρευνῶντες πράγματα· καὶ κλαίει πολλάκις γυνὴ καὶ ὀδύρεται, ἀλλ'
οὖν οὐ τὸν προκείμενον (ἀλλότριος γὰρ), ἀλλὰ τὸν ἑαυτῆς τὸν προαπελθόντα, καὶ
γίνεται ἡ ἀλλοτρία ὑπόθεσις ἰδίων κακῶν ὑπόμνησις· οὕτως ὑμῶν ἕκαστος, ἀδελφοὶ,
ὅταν τὰ παρὰ τῶν ἁγίων κηρυττόμενα μανθάνῃ, ἰδιοποιείτω τὴν λέξιν, ὑπὲρ τῶν
ἰδίων τραυμάτων λέγων, Υἱὲ ∆αυῒδ, ἐλέησόν με· καὶ λεγέτω καὶ νῦν ἕκαστος ἀπὸ
τῶν ἰδίων κακῶν διεγειρόμενος, ὁ μὲν, ὅτι τυφλός ἐστι τὴν διάνοιαν, ὁ δὲ, ὅτι
κωφὴν ἔχει τὴν ψυχήν· ἄλλος, ὅτι χωλὸν ἔχει τὸν λογισμὸν, ἕτερος, ὅτι λεπρὰν ἔχει
τὴν γνώμην. Τὰ γὰρ πάθη, ἃ ἐθεράπευσεν ἐπὶ τῶν σωμάτων ὁ Χριστὸς, ταῦτα καὶ
59.601 ἐπὶ τῶν ψυχῶν γίνεται καὶ δεῖται τῆς ἄνωθεν βοηθείας. Ἔστι τυφλὴ ψυχὴ,
δεομένη ἀναβλέψεως, τυφλὴ ψυχὴ, ἡ νόμου θαυμάσια μὴ βλέπουσα, τυφλὴ ψυχὴ, ἡ
english: A discourse concerning the blind man whom Christ healed, and concerning Zacchaeus, and concerning judgment and almsgiving. Many and diverse are the teachings of the holy Scriptures, but one grace shines upon all, and one source of teaching is the Spirit of truth.

Whatever the law forbids, whatever the prophets teach, whatever the apostles proclaim, and whatever the Gospel of piety dictates, all flow from one generous and fruitful source, the Holy Spirit; and there is nothing solemn to say, nothing right to think, nor wonderful to do, without the Holy Spirit confirming the things said, thought, and done. For even if someone has a soul strengthened by a morsel of human wisdom and by human reasonings, but rejects the word of God, it is nothing, and it will be accounted as nothing. Therefore the prophet says: 'They have done away with the word of the Lord' (Isa 5:5). What wisdom is in them?

For us, then, the Scriptures of piety are the flowers of truth; and the flowers are many, but the meadow that feeds the flowers is one; the luminaries of the teaching are many, but the true light is one; the stars are many, but the heaven that carries the stars is one; the branches are many, but the root is one; the fingers are many, but the hand that writes through the fingers is one; the strings are many, but the lyre of the Spirit is one; the teachings are many, but the source of piety is one.

But I marvel how this blind man, not having read the law, not having passed through the prophets, not having encountered the Gospels, and not having been confirmed by the apostles, called upon the Savior of the inhabited world, saying, 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me' (Mk 10:47). From where did you learn to call these things, without having learned what you invoke? Deprived of sight, you did not read books; you did not occupy yourself with teachings, having one premise of life, the petition, rather than the addition; from where...

So he knew the light of the world, whom he neither saw in the heavens nor upon the earth, being deprived of sight. But truly that which was said by David was fulfilled in this: The Lord makes the blind wise (Psalm 146:8). There was a great crowd around Jesus, and the blind man did not know the light of truth, but he knew its operation; he seized it by intention, which the sight had not received.

What, he asks, does the crowd intend? They say to him, "Jesus the Nazarene is passing by" (Matthew 9:27). Oh, the wonder! Other things are being taught, and other things are being preached; he hears Jesus the Nazarene, but he does not call him Jesus the Nazarene, but Jesus the Son of David (Matthew 20:30). Those seeing from presumption were speaking, but the blind man was preaching from truth. "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" (Matthew 20:30).

Therefore, each one making the voice his own, let him pour out a confession from the heart, and let each one say this voice for himself, "Son of David, have mercy on me." And just as, brothers, when many go to mourning, and see a corpse lying there, and being wept over by its own [kin], all weep—some sharing in the mourning, others searching out their own matters; and often a woman wails and laments, but indeed not for the one lying there (for he is a stranger), but for her own one who has passed before, and the stranger becomes a hypothesis for the remembrance of one's own evils—so each of you, brothers, when he learns the things being preached by the saints, let him make the word his own, speaking on behalf of his own wounds, "Son of David, have mercy on me."

And let each one say it now, being awakened from his own evils: one, because his intellect is blind; another, because his soul is mute; another, because his reasoning is lame; another, because his opinion is leprous. For the sufferings which Christ healed upon the bodies, these also happen upon the souls, and they need help from above. τὸν μέλλοντα αἰῶνα μὴ καθορῶσα, τυφλὴ ψυχὴ, ἡ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ βλέπουσα,
τὴν δὲ θεότητα μὴ γνωρίζουσα. Ὅτι δὲ τυφλή ἐστιν ἡ ψυχὴ ἡ ἀγνοοῦσα τὰ περὶ
Θεοῦ, μαρτυρεῖ Ἡσαΐας λέγων· Καὶ ἐτυφλώθησαν οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ Θεοῦ. Πῶς
ἐτυφλώθησαν; Εἴδετε γὰρ, φησὶ, πλεονάκις, καὶ οὐκ ἐφυλάξασθε· ἀνεῳγμένα τὰ ὦτα,
καὶ οὐκ ἠκούσατε. Καὶ τίς τυφλὸς, ἀλλ' ἢ οἱ παῖδές μου; καὶ τίς κωφὸς, ἀλλ' ἢ οἱ
κυριεύοντες αὐτῶν; Καὶ ὁ Σωτὴρ βουλόμενος δεῖξαι τύφλωσιν διανοίας, Φαρισαίους
τυφλώττοντας περὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐλέγχει λέγων· Ἐάσατε αὐτοὺς, ὁδηγοί εἰσι τυφλοὶ
τυφλῶν· τυφλὸς δὲ τυφλὸν ἐὰν ὁδηγῇ, ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθρον ἐμπεσοῦνται. Κωφὴ δέ
ἐστιν ἡ ψυχὴ ἡ νόμου μὴ ὑπακούουσα, ἡ τὴν ∆εσποτικὴν φωνὴν παραγραφομένη,
κωφὴ οὐκ ἐκ φύσεως, ἀλλ' ἐκ προαιρέσεως. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο ἔλεγεν ὁ Σωτήρ· Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα
ἀκούειν, ἀκουέτω· οὐχ ὅτι τινὲς τῶν παρόντων οὐκ εἶχον ὦτα· (πῶς γὰρ ἂν
ἐσχόλαζον τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ, τὸ ὄργανον τῆς ἀκοῆς οὐκ ἔχοντες;) ἀλλὰ δείκνυσι
σαφῶς, ὅτι τὸ μὲν φαινόμενον οὖς πρὸς ἀκοὴν δεδημιούργηται, ἡ δὲ τῆς ψυχῆς
αἴσθησις πρὸς τὴν ἀκοὴν τοῦ θείου νόμου οὐ συναρμόζεται. Οὐδὲν οὖν ὄφελος τῆς
ἔξωθεν ἀκοῆς, ἀποκεκωφωμένης τῆς ἔσωθεν διανοίας. Λεπρός τίς ἐστι τῇ ψυχῇ, οὐχ
ὁ τὸ σῶμα ἀμαυρούμενος, ἀλλ' ὁ τὴν ψυχὴν σκοτιζόμενος. Τί γάρ ἐστι λέπρα ἐν
σώματι, ἀλλ' ἢ διπλοῦν χρῶμα; Τί ἐστι λέπρα ἐν ψυχῇ; ∆ιπλοῦς διαλογισμός. Οὐαὶ
ἁμαρτωλῷ ἐπιβαίνοντι ἐπὶ δύο τρίβους! Ὅταν τις ποτὲ μὲν πιστεύῃ, ποτὲ δὲ ἀπιστῇ,
καὶ ποτὲ μὲν πρὸς ἐλεημοσύνην ῥέπῃ, ποτὲ δὲ πρὸς ἀπανθρωπίαν, λεπρός ἐστι τὴν
ψυχὴν, οὐκ ἔχων χρῶμα ὑγιὲς, ἀλλὰ μεριζόμενος τὴν διάνοιαν· καὶ ὥσπερ μερίζει
λέπρα τὸ σῶμα, οὕτω μερίζει λογισμὸς πονηρὸς τὴν διάνοιαν. Ἕκαστος οὖν ὑπὲρ
τῶν ἑαυτοῦ τραυμάτων βοήσῃ, καὶ ἐπικαλέσηται Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἰατρὸν ψυχῶν καὶ
σωμάτων, καθὼς ἐβόα ὁ τυφλός· Υἱὲ ∆αυῒδ, ἐλέησόν με. Καὶ οἱ μὲν προάγοντες,
ἐπετίμων· ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐμποδίζεται ἡ παῤῥησία διὰ τῶν κωλυόντων. Οἶδεν ἡ πίστις πρὸς
πάντα μάχεσθαι, καὶ πάντα νικᾷν. Ἐπετίμων ἄνθρωποι, καὶ ὁ πιστὸς οὐχ
ὑποστέλλεται, ἀλλ' ἀκολουθεῖ τῷ ∆εσπότῃ, εἰδὼς, ὅτι καλὴ ἡ ὑπὲρ εὐσεβείας
ἀναίδεια. βʹ. Εἰ γὰρ ὑπὲρ χρημάτων ἀναιδεῖς πολλοὶ, ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας ψυχῆς οὐ
κάλλιστον τὴν καλὴν ἀναίδειαν ἐνδύσασθαι; Κελεύει αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀχθῆναι.
Ἔστησε τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν ἡ φωνὴ τοῦ μετὰ πίστεως ἐπικαλουμένου· ἐκέλευσε πρὸς
αὐτὸν ἀχθῆναι τὸν ἐγγίσαντα αὐτῷ τῇ πίστει πρότερον, καὶ πλησιάσαι τῷ σώματι.
Ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ἀχθῆναι, καί φησι, Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω, Οὐκ ἀργῶς ἐρωτᾷ·
ἠδύνατο γὰρ καὶ καθημένῳ τὴν ἴασιν πέμψαι, ἀλλ' Ἰουδαῖοι οἱ τὴν ἀλήθειαν
συκοφαντοῦντες, ἠδύναντο εἰπεῖν, ὡς ἐπὶ τοῦ ἐκ γενετῆς τυφλοῦ, Οὐκ ἔστιν οὗτος,
ἀλλ' ὅμοιος αὐτοῦ. Καλεῖ οὖν εἰς μέσον τῶν ἀγνωμόνων τὸ θέατρον τὸν
εὐεργετούμενον, ἵνα πρῶτον δείξῃ τὸ πήρωμα τῆς φύσεως, καὶ τότε γνωρίσῃ τὴν
αὐθεντίαν τῆς χάριτος. Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω; Ἐρωτᾷ ἐκεῖνον, διδάσκει δὲ τοὺς
παρόντας. Ὁ δὲ, Κύριε, φησὶν, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω. Βλέπε, ὅσα λαμβάνει ἐνέχυρα παρὰ
τοῦ τὴν θεραπείαν δεχομένου, ἵνα ἀποκλείσῃ τὴν συκοφαντίαν τῶν
πονηρευομένων. Λέγει οὖν, Πορεύου, ἡ πίστις σου ἔσωσέ σε. Ὁρᾷς, πῶς τὸ
προειρημένον ἡμῖν κατὰ τὴν προτεραίαν δι' αὐτῶν δείκνυται τῶν ἔργων; καὶ ὅτι
ἄπρατοι αἱ εὐεργεσίαι, καὶ πωλοῦνται τῇ πίστει; Οὐ δίδωσιν ἀργυρίου τὰς εὐεργεσίας
Ἰησοῦς, πωλεῖ δὲ αὐτὰς τῇ πίστει. Ἐὰν μὴ καταβάλῃς πίστιν, οὐ δέχῃ τὴν
εὐεργεσίαν· ἡ χάρις ἥπλωται, ἡ δὲ πίστις προέρχεται. Καὶ ὥσπερ πηγὴ μία, ἀντλοῦσι
δὲ ἐκ τῆς πηγῆς οἱ μὲν μικροῖς ἀγγείοις, οἱ δὲ μείζοσι, καὶ ὁ μὲν ὀλίγον ἀρύεται
ὕδωρ, ὁ δὲ πολὺ, οὐ τῆς πηγῆς μεριζούσης τὰ μέτρα, ἀλλ' ἑκάστου πρὸς τὸ οἰκεῖον
ἀγγεῖον ἀρυομένου· οὕτως ἡ χάρις ἥπλωται ὡς πηγὴ, ἡ πρόθεσις δὲ τοῦ
προσερχομένου ἀγγεῖον καὶ σκεῦος γίνεται τῆς χάριτος. Ἐὰν οὖν προσαγάγῃς πίστιν
ὀλίγην ὡς σκεῦος μικρὸν, μικρὰν ἀντλεῖς τὴν χάριν· ἐὰν δὲ μεγάλην προσαγάγῃς
τὴν διάνοιαν, μεγάλην ἀντλεῖς τὴν εὐεργεσίαν. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο ὁ Σωτὴρ λέγει, Πιστεύεις,
ὅτι δύναμαι τοῦτο ποιῆσαι; Ὁ δὲ, Ναὶ, Κύριε· καὶ ὁ 59.602 Σωτὴρ, Κατὰ τὴν πίστιν σου
γενηθήτω σοι. Ἐντεῦθεν ὁ Ἀπόστολος παρακελεύεται Κορινθίοις λέγων·
Πλατύνθητε ὑμεῖς, ἵνα δείξῃ, ὅτι τῇ πλατυνομένῃ διανοίᾳ πλατυτέρα ἡ χάρις
ἐπεισέρχεται· καὶ ὁ προφήτης, Ἄνοιξον τὸ στόμα σου, καὶ πληρώσω αὐτό. Οὐδὲν

δικαιοσύνης ἀνέτειλεν Ἰησοῦς, ἥπλωται πανταχοῦ ἡ ἀκτὶς νοητοῦ ἡλίου· καὶ ὁ μὲν
english: The soul is blind when it does not see the coming age, seeing the body of Christ but not knowing the divinity. That the soul is blind when it is ignorant of things concerning God, Isaiah testifies, saying: 'And the servants of God were blinded' (Isa 6:9). How were they blinded? For, he says, you have repeatedly failed to take heed, having open ears, and you did not hear. And who is blind, but my children? And who is deaf, but their rulers? And the Savior, desiring to show a blindness of the intellect, reproves the Pharisees who are blinding themselves concerning the truth, saying: 'Leave them, they are blind guides; and if a blind man guides a blind man, both will fall into a pit' (Matt 15:14).

The soul is deaf when it does not obey the Law, ignoring the Lord's voice; this deafness is not by nature, but by choice. For this reason the Savior said: 'He who has ears to hear, let him hear' (Matt 13:9); not because those present lacked ears (for how could they have occupied themselves with teaching without the organ of hearing?), but he clearly shows that while the ear is fashioned for hearing, the perception of the soul is not joined to the hearing of the divine Law. Therefore, there is no profit in external hearing if the inner intellect is blinded.

Someone is a leper to the soul, not one whose body is darkened, but one whose soul is obscured. For what is leprosy in the body, if not a double color? What is leprosy in the soul? A divided mind. Woe to the sinner who treads upon two paths! Whenever one at times believes and at times is unbelieving, and at times leans toward almsgiving and at times toward inhumanity, he is a leper in the soul, not possessing a healthy color, but being divided in his intellect; and just as leprosy divides the body, so an evil thought divides the intellect.

Let each one, then, cry out for his own wounds, and call upon Jesus, the healer of souls and bodies, just as the blind man cried out: 'Son of David, have mercy on me' (Mark 10:48). And some may go forward, rebuking [him]; but boldness is not hindered by those who obstruct. Faith knows how to fight against all things, and overcomes all things. Even if men rebuke, the believer does not shrink back, but follows the Lord, knowing that boldness for the sake of piety is beautiful. For if many are shameless for the sake of money, for the sake of the soul's salvation, there is nothing more beautiful than holy boldness.

Should he put on [clothes]? Jesus commands him to be brought. The voice of the one calling upon him with faith caused the Lord Jesus to stand. He commanded the one who previously approached him with faith to be brought, and to approach the body. He commanded him to be brought, and says, 'What do you want me to do for you?'

He does not ask idly; for it was possible even while sitting to send the healing, but the Jews, slandering the truth, were able to say, as if regarding one born blind, 'This is not such, but one like him.' Therefore, he calls the one being benefited into the midst of the ignorant as a theater, so that first he might show the protrusion of nature, and then recognize the authority of grace. 'What do you want me to do for you?' He asks him, but teaches those present. And he says, 'Lord, that I may receive sight.'

See how much he receives in his hands from the one receiving the cure, so as to shut away the slander of the wicked. He says therefore, 'Go, your faith has saved you.' Do you see how the previously mentioned thing is shown to us through their works? And that the benefits are not idle, but are sold by faith? Jesus does not give the benefits for silver, but sells them by faith. If you do not cast in faith, you do not receive the benefit; grace is spread out, but faith proceeds.

And so that no one might suppose him to suffer through weakness, and not to endure through philanthropy, before he enters into Jerusalem, he looks at a fig tree. And he went away, he says, seeking fruit from it, and did not find. And as he did not find, he rebuked, saying: 'May fruit never come from you for an age.' What sin did the fig tree commit? For does it not have fruitfulness by rational authority? Is it not that when the Creator wills, he provides energy to the fruitfulness? Furthermore, it was not the season of figs; for this the Gospel testifies. Which of these common men, or surely not God, demands fruit at an unseasonable time? Did you not establish the seasons, O Creator? Did you not give seasons and times to fruitfulness? What then do you demand beyond the season which you appointed? The sinless one with sinners, the fountain of righteousness with the matter of injustice; for matter of injustice is greed. And see the wonderful thing: immediately Zacchaeus, standing before the door, says: 'Lord, I give half of my possessions to the poor' (Luke 19:8). You have not yet been taught, and you obey? You have not yet learned, and you have kept it? The Savior said nothing, nothing he taught, nothing about almsgiving he proposed, not love of the poor he commanded then, but he was silent, and by resting he enlightened; and just as a sun entering through the rays into a house, not by a word it enlightens, but by that energy it shines; so also the Savior, having entered, with the rays of righteousness cut off the path of injustice; 'For the light shines in the darkness' (John 1:5), as the evangelist says.

'Lord, I give half of my possessions to the poor' (Luke 19:8). Well he divides the greed, he cuts the injustice. 'The half of my possessions.' Everything whole is strong, but being cut is weak. 'The half of my possessions.' Oh, the beautiful voice, conquering nature, but rather conquering habit! For habit is a second nature. He cut off greed, he recognized the truth.

'I give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have wronged or slandered anyone, I give back fourfold' (Luke 19:8). Here it is necessary to pay precise attention, because the wealth of Zacchaeus was not from injustice only, but also from paternal inheritance.

english: Regarding possessions: if they were from injustice, how could he pay back fourfold what he took? For what does he say: 'If I have wronged anyone, I restore fourfold'? Even if he agreed with lawlessness, he also knew the law; for the law commands the thief to pay back the theft fourfold (Exodus 22:1). If anyone, he says, steals a sheep and is found out, he shall give four sheep. God quadruples the punishment, or rather the loss, so that even if one does not fear the law, the loss may be felt; for many, not respecting the law, respect the loss. He therefore condemns himself, not expecting the verdict of the law, but becoming a law unto himself; for law does not lie upon the righteous.

The Savior, having received this voice, says: 'Today salvation has come to this house' (Luke 19:9). He justified himself, not because he simply saw Christ, but because he obeyed the laws of Christ. Today salvation has come to this house, because this man also is a son of Abraham. Before doing the works of Abraham, he does not call him a son of Abraham, but calls him Zacchaeus by the bare appellation; but when he fulfilled the works of the patriarch, promising charity and the restitution of the injustice, then he says: 'And this man also is a son of Abraham.'

And we therefore, brothers, even if we are Christians and are called so, nothing demonstrates us as Christians in this way as the work of truth. Let us not therefore outdo the appellation with our works, but let us make the faith venerable with our works. We were called sons of Abraham through faith (Galatians 3:7); let us be called sons of Abraham through good works. For what he said, it is not the nobility of the body that is sought, but the following of the ways. For this reason Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the patriarchs rejected the synagogue, because they did not inherit the faith of the fathers; Abraham rejected his own kin because they did not follow the faith; Isaac, Jacob, and all the patriarchs rejected them too; the

For having denied God, nature also denies. And what word will testify that Abraham denied the Jews, so that we might not be bold as if against enemies, but as if reproving those who have sinned? The blessed Jeremiah says on behalf of the people: 'Lord, have mercy on us; the mountain and the city, which our fathers blessed, became consumed by fire; you, Lord, have mercy on us, because Abraham did not know us, and Israel did not recognize us; you, Lord, spare us' (Jeremiah 49:1). Because, he says, those on whom we take pride were alienated from us, and they denied our race, you have mercy on us, conquering all through philanthropy. Have mercy on us, because Abraham did not know us (Genesis 25:17-18). For if our things were his own, he would not have interceded for his own children. He interceded for the Sodomites, and he was heard; and for his own interceding, was he not heard? Abraham did not know us. Abraham denies the strangers in his ways, but he makes the strangers, as I said, to be strangers in race, yet kin in piety. For this reason the Scripture, desiring to show to the Jews that whoever adopts the ways of those, receives also their claim, says: 'Your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite, and your sister a Sodomite' (Deuteronomy 7:3). See how he constructs kinship from the ways. Because he thought of the things of the Sodomites, a sister of Sodom heard, a daughter of the Canaanites heard; and thus it was being shown not the race that is righteous, but the character that is venerable. But I think that the Canaanite and the Amorite denies the kinship; and when he sees the god-fighters and those who approach him as strangers to piety, he denies, and the Canaanite does not accept to be called the father of the ungodly. Why does he deny? If you insult a Canaanite and say, 'Your father is a Canaanite,' he will say: 'Is this my son, having denied the faith of the fathers?' I am not faithless, even if I am a Canaanite; for the Canaanite woman crying out, 'Son of David, have mercy on me' (Matthew 15:22), will testify to my faith.

And if he is his mother, then the one who has honored righteousness by the designation is a son of the mother. Let every soul therefore...
A mother of Christ according to disposition. How a mother of Christ? Every soul labors in pain for him, the Christ; but if it is not transformed by piety, it cannot be called a mother of Christ.

When you receive the word of Christ and fashion it in your mind; just as you transform it in the mother of thought, so you are called a good mother of him. And so that you may know that in each one Christ is being formed and becomes a mother of Christ—I say indeed of the word of the Christ, that each of us is the soul, as Paul says: 'My children, whom I again labor for, until Christ is formed in you' (Galatians 4:19).

Did you work righteousness? You formed Christ in the soul. Did you grant alms? You formed the character of the truth. It is not that Christ is formed according to each one; for he calls the word of piety 'Christ', through which we receive the character of the truth. Did you grant alms? You formed Christ. Did you do righteousness? The character of the truth was formed.

Therefore it is necessary to attend to how one must make Christ a brother. Take him as a partner of your things. Do you not want to grant everything to him? Even if you give half, give it to him like Zacchaeus (Luke 19:8). For to him, he says, Zacchaeus gave, not to the poor. But listen: he who shows mercy to the poor lends to God (Proverbs 19:17). Giving to the poor, you have given to Christ (Matthew 25:40).

Do you not know that what is given to himself he receives back? Do you not know what a fearful judgment he has written, saying: 'When the Son of Man comes in the regeneration, he will set the sheep at the right hands, but the goats at the left; and he will say to those at the right hands, Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you, because I was hungry, and you gave me to eat' (Matthew 25:34-36)? See how he who lends through the poor acknowledges the debt: 'I was hungry, and you fed me; I was naked, and you clothed me.'

Surely, by clothing the naked in the apparent form, you clothe Christ in the truth. Clothe Christ, so that he may clothe you in the day of judgment; cover him, so that he may cover you in the day of wrath. Listen to David saying: 'Cover me in the secret of his tent' (Psalm 27:5). Covering is necessary; that fearful fire seizes, the unavoidable Gehenna; and if the hand of Christ does not cover, that foreign fire will make known. He knows how to take hold of what is foreign, he knows how to honor the holy, he knows how to respect piety, and he takes hold of impiety.

english: the Christ's judgment seat

When the Son of Man comes in his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel (Matt 19:28). Books will be opened. Books, in which the worthless things are written, in which the good things are written, in which each person's life is recorded.

And it is called a book, not because it is skin before God and letters; but because, since the book of memory is an instrument for you, it records the memory of God just as in a book; for God has no need of a book; for to God, memory is the book. Not that we, humans, reading prophets, apostles, and Gospels, carry the memory in our heart without a book, yet the God of the book is in need; the source of memory has no need of a book. There the virtuous works are written, there the worthless things are written.

Do not fear the proverb; even if your evil works are recorded, they can be erased through good works; just as if someone's name is written through piety, but he denies it by his ways, the proverb does not make the writing stay; for it is erased. So that you may learn that the one written through piety and cast out through negligence is erased, David says concerning the Jews who were once written and later erased: 'Let them be blotted out from the book of the living, and let them not be written with the righteous' (Ps 69:6). Just as the unfaithful are blotted out, so the faithful are written. Listen to Paul saying: 'Greet the brothers whom we love, and Clement and the other fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life' (Phil 4:3).

Let us fear that book; fear, lest your sins be recorded; understand how you prepare yourself for judgment, if the memoranda against you are opened before a ruler, accusing you of injustice, charging you with madness; understand how much fear, how much trembling, how the limbs shake, how everything within seethes, of a man judging. If there is such fear from a man judging, who will be able to endure that fear, by which the Master of all is about to judge the inhabited world? We say these things, not that we may frighten, but that we may bring to sobriety. Let money not be preferred over Christ; let injustice and greed not be preferred over God. Have you heard of the things previously mentioned, that prosperity lasts only until the grave? These things were given to us yesterday.

english: He was training himself. What are you waiting for, that the tomb becomes the end of your life? Wait for the tomb to become the end of your life, so that through the present one you may be transformed into the coming one; love works of righteousness; it is a tomb in which we are being dissolved, a tomb in which the earthly vessel is being made to vanish.

Let us flee the coming judgment, brothers, I beg you. These things must be said by those suffering, and must be heard by those suffering; let us take up a longing for righteousness. See how the prophet cries out: 'Woe is me toward the day of the Lord, for the day of the Lord is near' (Zephaniah 1:15). If a prophet trembles remembering the day, shall we, who are responsible for myriads of sins, remember without fear?

Let us dissemble the judge through repentance, let us blot out our sins, let us fear that terrible voice saying, 'Whosoever denies me before men (not denying by word, but denying by ways/manner, denies), I will deny him' (Matthew 10:33), I too will deny him before my Father. Whosoever should confess me, I too will confess him before my Father. If the words being examined are fearsome, are the things being seen not rather more fearsome?

Consider, brother, the judge of the inhabited world sitting, angels standing by him, archangels guarding, the Cherubim glorifying, the super-cosmic powers, the super-celestial armies, and in all these, patriarchs, prophets, apostles, evangelists, martyrs, and the kings in the world, rulers, judges, the powerful, the rich, the poor, the commoners, the wise, all these standing before the tribunal, and speaking the judge before so many heavenly and earthly witnesses, and denying the others before the Father: 'For I will deny him,' he says, 'him who denies me, before my Father.'

Consider him saying: 'Father, this one has exhausted my faith, this one has persecuted my own, this one has insulted my Church, this one has pillaged my own, this one has twisted the Word, this one has trampled the proclamation.' He says these things, not teaching those who do not know the Father, but accusing the enemy through indictment. Consider the judge saying, when he calls those of the earth who are bound in fetters (For to bind, he says, the rulers...

(those in the fields, and the glorious ones in iron shackles), the judged ones standing with fear, the powerful ones, and the Savior saying: 'These perverted my word of truth, these wrote against my law, these invalidated my dogma, these killed my apostles, these tortured my martyrs.'

Consider, while the King speaks, how the standing angels cry out terribly, threaten frighteningly, already consuming the sinner with their gaze; consider the angels indignant, the archangels moved, the powers shaken, the Father indignant, the Holy Spirit being angry, Him being cast out with great shame, being cast out not only from salvation but also being exiled to condemnation. For it is not only fearful not to be saved, nor to reign, but also to be handed over to the fire (Matt 25:41). He who confesses in me, I will confess in him (Luke 18:14).

Consider how much glory, how much boasting, how much a crown, when the judge says: 'This one kept my word, this one proclaimed my faith, this one confirmed my word, this one did not overlook the poor, this one trampled greed and prized righteousness, this one laughed at the world as if it did not exist and loved the coming world, this one pursued my kingdom (Matt 6:33); this one honored my word'; honor him, Father. When we say these things in a figurative way, we do not divide the value, nor do we dissolve the authority, but the indignation of the Judge is shown by the form of the category; and all these things happen for the salvation of those confessing and for the condemnation of those being unfaithful.

And what is more fearful of all is when you consider Michael and Gabriel standing, and all the angelic hosts sitting, the sons of Zebedee sitting, Paul and Peter sitting, those from among men, while angels stand with fear, and men sit with boldness. Consider the standing angels and the fishermen and the tax collectors sitting, and let us say also with them: 'How great is the multitude of your kindness, Lord!'
